name: Cosmetic contact lens handling tint

card.summary: A faint blue or green visibility tint added to contact lenses so they are easy to see and pick up, which helps wearers keep lenses clean and correctly placed while the tint stays nearly invisible on the eye.
card.note: Distinct from colour-changing or circle lenses, which are cosmetic tints meant to alter eye appearance.

quick.overview:
A handling tint is a very light colour, commonly pale blue, added to many clear contact lenses so they can be seen in a case, on a fingertip or in solution. It makes lenses easier to locate and insert so wearers can keep their eyes looking natural and avoid dropping lenses.

The tint is made faint enough to be nearly invisible when the lens is on the eye. It differs from cosmetic tints that change the look of the iris, such as colour-enhancing and circle lenses.
quick.how: Wearers do not need to do anything; the tint is part of the lens. It is simply seen against a surface when the lens is handled. Some lens makers have also patented designs where the tint fades in disinfecting solution to signal that a lens has been worn too long.
quick.risks: The handling tint itself is a minor design feature. Contact lenses in general can cause redness, irritation or infection, and cosmetic lenses worn without correction still need a proper fitting according to Wikipedia's contact lens article.

lead: A handling tint, also called a visibility tint, is a light tint applied to many corrective contact lenses so that the otherwise almost transparent lens is slightly visible and easier to find and handle.[1] One-day disposable lenses with a pale blue tint are a common example.[1]

For appearance, the point is that a wearer can place lenses accurately and keep them clean, while the eye still looks uncovered, because the tint is too faint to colour the iris. It is separate from cosmetic tints that change eye colour or enlarge the iris, such as circle lenses.[1]

Lens makers have also used the handling tint as a signal. Patents from 1993 and 1994 describe lenses whose tint changes in an oxidant disinfectant over the expected lifetime of the lens so that the wearer can tell when the lens is overworn.[2][3]

chain: Faint tint makes the lens visible when handled
Easier, cleaner insertion and fewer dropped lenses
angle.text: The tint makes lenses easy to see and pick up and is nearly invisible once worn, so wearers can use contact lenses in place of glasses without a visible colour on the eye.

paras: Clear lenses are hard to see in solution or on a fingertip, so manufacturers add a light tint to most corrective lenses to make them easy to locate.[1] Cosmetic tints are a separate category: some fully cover the iris for a colour change, some enhance natural colour, and circle lenses extend the iris onto the white of the eye with a dark ring.[1]

A patent family filed in the early 1990s describes applying a handling tint in an amount chosen so that, after repeated soaking in an oxidant disinfecting solution over the lens's expected life, the tint visibly changes and tells the user the lens is overworn.[2][3]

timeline.event: Patent describes overworn-lens signalling using a handling tint.[2]
